newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia says seeks more forest jobs.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia says seeks more forest jobs.

text.p: British Columbia vowed on Monday to create 21,000 new jobs in its forest sector by 2001 and held out the promise of reduced bureacracy for forest companies.

The government and industry officials have been negotiating an accord designed to satisfy the province's demands for new forest jobs and respond to forest companies' complaints that regulation is creating excessive costs.
"The jobs and timber accord must...assist the industry as it weathers cyclical changes in world markets," the government said in a speech from the throne.
The speech was read by Lieutenant Governor Garde Gardom, the Queen's representative in the province, at the start of a new sitting of the provincial legislature.

The accord must involve a number of initiatives "including a reduction in bureaucracy and red tape and an increase in the level and types of investment undertaken by Forest Renewal B.C.," the government said. Forest Renewal is a provincial fund created to revitalize the sector's economic base.
Premier Glen Clark has threatened to remove companies' logging rights if they did not create new jobs.
Forest companies including Canada's biggest, MacMillan Bloedel Ltd, have complained that the cost of doing business in British Columbia has soared due to recent stricter regulations.
Executives have said the results of their talks with the province on the jobs and timber accord may be known by the end of March.
